links.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-5 emergency management responses with guidelines and specialist gold standard
links.effect: High agreement (5/5) in 5 scenarios (33.3%), moderate (4/5) in 7 (46.7%), low (≤3/5) in 3 (20.0%); omissions of scoring systems and mortality risk emphasis.
links.quote: High agreement (5/5) was observed in 5 scenarios (33.3%), moderate agreement (4/5) in 7 scenarios (46.7%), and low agreement (≤ 3/5) in 3 scenarios (20.0%).

links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-5 responses (FRES, FKGL, SMOG, CLI)
links.effect: FRES 40.5 ± 2.5; FKGL 11.6 ± 1.2; SMOG 10.9 ± 0.8; CLI 10.9 ± 0.8, indicating moderately technical language.
links.quote: Readability analyses showed that responses contained a moderate amount of technical language (FRES score = 40.5 ± 2.5; FKGL score = 11.6 ± 1.2; SMOG score = 10.9 ± 0.8; and CLI score = 10.9 ± 0.8).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates ChatGPT (referred to as ChatGPT-5) responses against clinical expert answers across 15 simulated obstetric and gynecological emergency scenarios, testing accuracy, readability, and safety, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
